exposure: Country of origin (grouped by baseline CS levels)
cohort: The study included first deliveries among 23,147 immigrants from 10 countries and 385,306 non-immigrants in Norway between 1990 and 2009.
finding: Among immigrants from countries with low baseline caesarean section (CS) levels, longer length of residence in Norway was associated with an increased risk of planned CS, while immigrants from high CS level countries consistently had higher emergency CS rates irrespective of residence duration.
mod_finding: Length of residence in Norway and country of origin were found to significantly influence the risk of both planned and emergency caesarean sections among immigrants.
